question: Volunteers in a brain scanner tasted one wine, labelled once at $90 and once at $10. What changed?
options: Only what they claimed to prefer
Their pleasure and its brain signal
answer: Their pleasure and its brain signal. In a 2008 Caltech study, the same wine labelled $90 was rated more pleasant than when labelled $10, and activity rose in the medial orbitofrontal cortex, an area that tracks how pleasant things feel. The price did not just change the opinion; it changed what the brain recorded.
move: A price on the label is part of what the senses report.
ask: Would I enjoy my favourite things as much if I did not know what they cost?
trap: Assuming people only said they liked it, to seem discerning.
reference: Plassmann, O'Doherty, Shiv & Rangel, Marketing actions can modulate neural representations of experienced pleasantness, PNAS, 2008
